title: Coherent mates of squares along enhanced equivalences
statement:
Use the universes, enhanced categories, coherent functors and coherent natural equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\mathscr A,\mathscr B,\mathscr A',\mathscr B'$ be enhanced categories. Specify adjoint equivalences $L:\mathscr A\rightleftarrows\mathscr B:R$ and $L':\mathscr A'\rightleftarrows\mathscr B':R'$, meaning coherent functors with units $\eta:\mathrm{id}\to RL$, $\eta':\mathrm{id}\to R'L'$ and counits $\epsilon:LR\to\mathrm{id}$, $\epsilon':L'R'\to\mathrm{id}$, all natural equivalences with specified coherent triangle identities. Let $V:\mathscr A\to\mathscr A'$ and $U:\mathscr B\to\mathscr B'$ be coherent functors and let $\alpha:L'V\simeq UL$ be a specified coherent natural equivalence. Composition below is written in the usual right-to-left order.

The composite
$$\theta_{U,V}:VR\xrightarrow{\eta'VR}R'L'VR\xrightarrow{R'\alpha R}R'ULR\xrightarrow{R'U\epsilon}R'U$$
is a coherent natural equivalence. The space of coherent transformations $\theta:VR\to R'U$ equipped with a homotopy
$$\epsilon'U\circ L'\theta\simeq U\epsilon\circ\alpha R$$
is contractible. Here the space means the homotopy fiber, over the specified right side, of postcomposition with $\epsilon'U$ after applying $L'$ to transformations in the enhanced functor categories. The displayed composite, with its mate homotopy from the triangle identities, is a point of that space.

For the identity square this mate is coherently the identity of $R$. Given a second such square $U':\mathscr B'\to\mathscr B''$, $V':\mathscr A'\to\mathscr A''$, $\alpha':L''V'\simeq U'L'$ and an adjoint equivalence $L''\dashv R''$, put $\alpha''=(U'\alpha)\circ(\alpha'V)$. Then the mate of the pasted square is coherently equivalent to
$$\theta_{U',V'}U\circ V'\theta_{U,V}:V'VR\longrightarrow R''U'U.$$
These comparisons are natural in coherent transformations of squares and satisfy all unit, associativity and higher pasting compatibilities for every finite composable string of squares. The vertical functors $U,V$ need not themselves be equivalences.

proof.text:
Work in the enhanced functor categories of the statement. Composition and whiskering retain their coherent simplices by the functor-category calculus and simplicial composition lemma. Define $\theta=(R'U\epsilon)\circ(R'\alpha R)\circ(\eta'VR)$. Its three factors are equivalences: the specified units, counits and $\alpha$ are equivalences, and functors preserve inverse edges and their inverse triangles. Thus their composite is an equivalence. To check the required homotopy, expand $\epsilon'U\circ L'\theta$. Naturality of $\epsilon'$ first moves $U\epsilon$ and then $\alpha R$ past the counit, giving
$$\epsilon'U\circ L'\theta\simeq U\epsilon\circ\alpha R\circ\epsilon'L'VR\circ L'\eta'VR\simeq U\epsilon\circ\alpha R.$$
The last homotopy is the specified triangle identity for $L'\dashv R'$, whiskered by $VR$. These are simplices in the functor categories, rather than equations only in their homotopy categories.

source.place: Opening compactification transport, inherited dense-comparison foundation, former step 12 (generic enhanced mate assertion).

proof.text: Let $T=\operatorname{Map}(VR,R'U)$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathscr B,\mathscr A')$ and $C=\operatorname{Map}(L'VR,U)$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathscr B,\mathscr B')$. Both are Kan complexes by the functor-category calculus. Whiskering by $L'$ gives a functor equivalence between these functor categories: whiskering by $R'$ is its quasi-inverse, with unit and counit obtained by whiskering $\eta',\epsilon'$. It therefore induces an equivalence $T\to\operatorname{Map}(L'VR,L'R'U)$. Postcomposition with the equivalence $\epsilon'U$ is an equivalence of mapping spaces, since postcomposition with its inverse supplies the inverse map and the inverse triangles supply the inverse homotopies (simplicial composition lemma). Their composite is exactly $f:T\to C$, $\theta\mapsto\epsilon'U\circ L'\theta$. The homotopy-fiber criterion makes its fiber over $b=U\epsilon\circ\alpha R$ contractible. Step 1 gives a specified point in this fiber, including its compatibility homotopy.

proof.text: For the identity square use the same adjoint equivalence on both rows, $U=\mathrm{id}$, $V=\mathrm{id}$ and $\alpha=\mathrm{id}_L$. Then the formula of Step 1 becomes $(R\epsilon)\circ(\eta R)$. The specified triangle identity for $L\dashv R$ identifies this with $\mathrm{id}_R$. Composition with the identity factors uses the degeneracies of the simplicial composition lemma. This supplies a point with its compatibility homotopy; Step 2 identifies it coherently with the identity-square mate.

source.place: Opening compactification transport, inherited dense-comparison foundation, former step 12 (generic enhanced mate assertion).

proof.text:
Write $\theta$ and $\theta'$ for the two mates, and put $q=(\theta'U)\circ(V'\theta)$. To compare $q$ with the pasted mate it suffices to exhibit its point in the same compatibility fiber of Step 2. First apply the compatibility homotopy for $\theta'$, whiskered by $U$, and then naturality of $\alpha'$ with respect to $\theta$:
$$\epsilon''U'U\circ L''q\simeq U'\epsilon'U\circ\alpha'R'U\circ L''V'\theta\simeq U'\epsilon'U\circ U'L'\theta\circ\alpha'VR.$$
The compatibility homotopy for $\theta$ now gives
$$\epsilon''U'U\circ L''q\simeq U'U\epsilon\circ U'\alpha R\circ\alpha'VR=U'U\epsilon\circ\alpha''R.$$
All regroupings and naturality homotopies are coherent compositions in the functor categories. Thus $q$ and the pasted mate, together with these witnesses, lie in the same contractible fiber; a path there is the required comparison. The order of application is $V'\theta$ first, followed by $\theta'U$.

proof.text: Retain the compatibility witnesses throughout. The computations in Steps 1 and 4 are compositions and restrictions of simplices and are therefore natural in coherent families of squares. Here is the relative choice argument needed for higher coherence. For each map $f$ of Step 2 replace it by its mapping-path fibration $P(f)\to C$. The fiber criterion makes this a trivial Kan fibration, so it lifts every boundary inclusion $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$. Over a specified compatible family on the boundary this supplies the entire next simplex, not merely a path between its vertices. For a finite string, impose the mate compatibility condition at each interval of that string, starting with intervals of length one. Pasting shorter intervals gives the compatible target at the next interval by the calculation in Step 4. Pull back the corresponding trivial fibration along this target family; its boundary lifting property is preserved, since a lift in a pullback is precisely a lift in the original map with the specified base. For finitely many intervals repeat these lifts in increasing length. Coherent composition choices are made in the same relative way using the trivial Kan fibrations of the simplicial composition lemma. Starting with the identity and binary comparisons above, lift successive simplex boundaries; the edges are the comparisons, the next simplices identify their two associativity composites, and the subsequent boundaries give every higher compatibility. Degeneracies prescribe the units. Because the construction accepts arbitrary parameter simplices of transformations of squares, the same lifts give naturality together with its higher compatibilities. This proves the asserted simultaneous coherence for every finite string.

That proof gives only transport context and no mate theorem, so the item's agent-written origin and WANTED line are correct. Typing checks out: theta: VR->R'U and alpha''=U'alpha o alpha'V : L''V'V->U'UL. I recomputed the Step 1 homotopy (naturality of eps' twice, then the L'-|R' triangle identity whiskered by VR) and the Step 4 pasting chain (theta' compatibility whiskered by U, naturality of alpha' along theta, U' applied to theta's compatibility); both give the stated result. Step 2: postcomposition with L' is a functor equivalence, the calculus gives equivalences on mapping spaces, the spine lemma makes postcomposition with eps'U an equivalence, and the fiber criterion gives contractible homotopy fibers; this fiber matches def-cbc's homotopy fiber. Step 3 reduces to R eps o eta R ~ id_R. Step 5 is a valid relative boundary-filling argument from the trivial Kan fibrations; its higher-coherence clause is informal, which I note for stage 2 only. Small cases: identity square, nerves of ordinary categories with non-invertible U and V, and empty categories. Parent orientation (L=p*, V=v*, U=u*, alpha=id) is correct. Duplicate search: lem-coef-dg-mate-transpose and lem-coef-dg-mate-pasting are D(Z)-enriched, in another unit, general adjunctions and give no contractible fiber, so they are not duplicates. There are no new nodes, no SGA citation, the route stays inside sk-prop-sf-cbc, proof_deps equals the union of the step uses, there is no cycle, and the Mathlib searches cover three kinds with the mateEquiv hits correctly judged 1- or 2-categorical.
